1.note: The author does not indicate exactly when Yahweh spoke the following words. It may have been before or after the events narrated in the previous chapter. Avoid implying a time relationship with the previous section. Alternate translation: [One day, Yahweh spoke]

2.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם כִּ֣י תָבֹ֗אוּ אֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵי⁠כֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֥ן לָ⁠כֶֽם
2.note: In 15:2–16, Yahweh tells Moses to speak for him to the Israelites. To do so, he uses a quote inside another quote. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. See the book introduction for more information, and see the UST for an example.

The term **and say to them** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.
In a context such as this, your language might say “come” instead of **go**. Alternate translation: [When you come]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **land** that is characterized by the fact that the Israelites would have **dwellings** there. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to the land where you will dwell] or [to the land where your houses will be]

God is using the present tense **am giving** to describe something that is going to happen in the future in order to show that the event is certain to happen. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use the future tense. Alternate translation: [I am about to give]

The implication is that “sacrifice” refers to any of the many kinds of animal sacrifices that the Israelites could offer. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [or another sacrifice]

The author is using **to make extraordinary a vow** as a common expression of his culture to mean “to fulfill a vow.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to fulfill a vow]

The implication is that these sacrifices were made at the annual festivals that Yahweh had appointed for Israel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [or at your yearly festivals]

The implication is that people burned the sacrifices in order for Yahweh to enjoy their smell. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the chapter introduction. Alternate translation: [to burn it to make a smell that pleases Yahweh]

A **tenth** means one part out of ten equal parts, and a **fourth** means one part out of four equal parts.

The **hin** was equivalent to about four liters or one gallon, so a fourth of a hin was about one liter or one quart. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

Alternate translation: [sojourner sojourns with you, or if anyone else {is} in your midst for your generations] (2) one group of people, with the second clause further defining the first. Alternate translation: [a sojourner sojourns with you in your midst for your generations] (3) two different groups of people, “sojourners” who are temporary residents and others who are permanent residents. 28.q: וְ⁠כִפֶּ֣ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֗ן עַל־הַ⁠נֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַ⁠שֹּׁגֶ֛גֶת בְּ⁠חֶטְאָ֥ה בִ⁠שְׁגָגָ֖ה לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לְ⁠כַפֵּ֥ר עָלָ֖י⁠ו

Alternate translation: [And they put him under guard] or [And they kept him in a place for retraining people]

38.q: וְ⁠עָשׂ֨וּ לָ⁠הֶ֥ם צִיצִ֛ת עַל־כַּנְפֵ֥י בִגְדֵי⁠הֶ֖ם לְ⁠דֹרֹתָ֑⁠ם וְ⁠נָֽתְנ֛וּ
38.note: Yahweh switches from the third person (**they**) to second person (“you”) in verse 39. This shows that Moses was supposed to tell the Israelites what they should do, and then tell them directly what the purpose was. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate all of these statements in the second person. Alternate translation: [And you shall make for yourselves a tassel on the hems of your clothes for your generations, and you shall put]

A **tassel** is a kind of decorative tuft of threads or cords that hangs down. If your readers would not be familiar with what a tassel is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a tuft of threads … on the tuft of threads]

The author assumes that readers will know that a typical garment in ancient Israel was a rectangular cloth with four corners at the hems or edges. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [at each of the four places where the edges of your clothes meet]

The implication is that the blue cord needs to be attached to the tassel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall add to each tassel of the hem a cord of blue]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **tassel** that is attached to **the hem**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on the tassel at each of the hems]

39.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֣ה לָ⁠כֶם֮ לְ⁠צִיצִת֒ וּ⁠רְאִיתֶ֣ם אֹת֗⁠וֹ וּ⁠זְכַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה
39.note: The implication is that the Israelites will remember the commandments when they see the tassels. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [all my commandments]

Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [after your what you think and after what you see] or [after your thoughts and after your desires]

41.note: In a context such as this, your language might say “took” instead of **brought**. Alternate translation: [took you out]
